citation: Barker, M.K., et al. (2021) Improved LOLA elevation maps for south pole landing sites: Error estimates and their impact on illumination conditions. Planetary and Space Science 203:105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119
where: Table 2, page 8 of the accepted manuscript (NTRS 20205009660); RoI centroids are the + symbols in Fig. 14; section 5 gives the method
transcribed: 2026-10-02, by hand from pdftotext -layout of the file pinned in sources.yaml; X and Y are negative in the paper (a minus sign extracts as a replacement character in the plain-text export), in km, in the south-polar stereographic frame of the 5 m DEM of Site 1 (the Site01 tile centre is at about -10.99, -11.99 km)
quantity: Site 1, 100 clones of the 5 m LDEM, 2024-01-01 to 2026-01-01, hourly. avg_ill_1 is the 1st percentile over the clones of the average visible fraction of the Sun's disk, in percent; lcip_1_days the 1st percentile of the longest continuous illumination period (any part of the disk visible); lcsp_99_days the 99th percentile of the longest continuous shadow period. A: percentiles after averaging the RoI for each clone; B: per pixel then averaged over the RoI; C: A but counting only the most illuminated pixel of the RoI at each hourly step
regions_of_interest: connected pixels with nominal average illumination above 70% at 1 m and area above 2500 m2 in the new (nominal) LDEM
method_in_paper: horizon method of Mazarico et al. (2011), 720 azimuths 0.5 degrees apart; nested grid: 5 m LDEM below 5 km, 80 m LDEM from 5 to 100 km, 240 m LDEM beyond; hourly steps; Sun a 2-D extended source with limb darkening at 550 nm; visible fraction found by dividing the disk horizontally at the horizon elevation at the disk centre's azimuth; MOON_ME of DE421
